mainEntity.name: Do you provide rehabilitation clinic cleaning in Braintree, MA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Braintree (Norfolk County) is one of the 109 Massachusetts cities and towns we serve. It is about 30 miles east of our Marlborough base in a straight line. Every engagement starts with a free on-site assessment; call (978) 307-8107.

mainEntity.name: Which Braintree ZIP codes do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: All of them: 02184, 02185. If your facility sits on a town line, tell us the street address and we will confirm.

mainEntity.name: Which nearby towns do you also serve?

acceptedAnswer.text: The closest served towns to Braintree are Weymouth (about 2.9 mi), Randolph (about 3.3 mi), Quincy (about 3.8 mi). See the full list on our service areas page.

mainEntity.name: Which surfaces should be cleaned more often than everything else?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ones closest to the patient and touched most: plinth rails and adjustment levers, parallel bars, treadmill handrails and consoles, cable grips, dumbbell handles, door hardware, and treatment room light switches. CDC Core Practices 5b and Section II item A of the Infection Prevention Checklist call for high-touch surfaces near the patient to sit on a more frequent schedule than general environmental surfaces. In practice that means a mid-day high-touch circuit through the gym on top of the terminal clean, and that mid-day circuit is where most clinics have a gap.

mainEntity.name: Can you clean and maintain our whirlpool or hydrotherapy tank?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Tank filling, draining, chemical treatment, and disinfection are clinical equipment protocols set by the tank manufacturer, with their own logs and competency requirements, and they belong to your staff. We clean the room around it: floors, drains, walls, benches, handrails, and door hardware, which is where wet-area soil actually accumulates. If the hydrotherapy area shows standing water, a slow drain, or degraded flooring, that goes into our report, because those are environmental conditions and raising them is our job.

mainEntity.name: How do I know your crew knows what it is doing in a clinical gym?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because training and competency validation are documented rather than assumed. Section I item B of the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist expects cleaning personnel to receive job-specific training and competency validation at hire and whenever procedures or products change. Our crews are trained on clean-to-dirty sequencing, color-coded microfiber, contact time discipline, and the specific products in your building, with records kept per person. Jeneva Thomas founded Dory's after 22 years of clinical experience, which is why the training is written around real findings rather than around a supply catalog.

Braintree rehabilitation clinics: how we clean

In a rehabilitation clinic, most cleaning failures happen at treatment tables, mats, therabands, free weights, exercise balls, parallel bars, treadmills. That is where our Braintree crews start, because the underlying risk is direct skin contact with shared equipment all day, with no barrier — MRSA and fungal transfer.

Facility types we clean under this service:

  • Physical Therapy
  • Occupational Therapy
  • Speech Therapy
  • Sports Medicine

Usually arranged with the clinic director (pt / ot / speech).

Rehabilitation clinics and senior care facilities are one of our core specialties — see how we clean them.

Inside a Braintree service visit

The surfaces we prioritise in Braintree

  • Treatment tables and plinths
  • Exercise mats
  • Free weights, dumbbells and kettlebells
  • Resistance bands and handles
  • Waiting-room seating
  • Restroom fixtures

How a visit runs

  1. Wipe down weights, bars and cardio equipment handles and consoles.
  2. Launder or replace reusable linens per the clinic's process — we do not take clinic linens off site unless contracted.
  3. Empty trash; sharps are rare but stay with the clinic's hauler if present.
  4. Damp-mop gym floors and vacuum carpeted areas.
  5. Log areas completed and any damaged equipment surfaces we notice.

How often

  • Restrooms and changing areas: daily or more often.
  • Waiting room: daily.
  • Periodic: equipment deep clean and high dusting.

Clinics with early-morning patients may prefer a pre-opening clean.

Records for your surveyors

  • Gym and treatment-room checklist
  • Product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
  • Signed service logs
  • Certificate of insurance

What inspectors cite — and how we prevent it

Real, published regulatory findings — every citation links to its source.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section I Environmental Cleaning item A

No written policies and procedures for routine cleaning and disinfection of the gym, treatment tables and shared equipment, including who is responsible for what.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section I item B

Cleaning staff have not received job-specific training and competency validation at hire and whenever procedures or products change.

CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices 5f

Clean and soiled equipment stored together, with no physical separation to prevent cross-contamination.

  • Will you clean the free weights and cardio equipment every visit?
  • How do you report a torn table cover that can no longer be disinfected?
